verified.notes: Installed from the packed tarball into a disposable isolated non-Desktop profile, composed with --dump-config, booted with a bounded real startup, exercised over the authenticated /api transport, generated one real image through the live Agnes API, downloaded its bytes through the media route, verified the record and artifact survive a restart, and verified deletion removes both. The Client half was then driven in a real headless Chrome against the owned DSH Web app over CDP (scripts/ui-check.mjs), with two deterministic image records seeded into the owned data directory (scripts/seed-fixture.mjs) so the gallery and viewer could be exercised without network, credentials or quota: the sidebar entry selects the studio page, the panel renders without a console error, the two-pane body is measured to be two columns side by side with the composer pinned to the left edge of the content column and the gallery taking the remaining width, the parameter controls render their model-derived values in the shape their option count calls for (a segmented control for four resolutions, chips for eight ratios), the Flash video model narrows the resolution list to 720P, the generate button is measured to sit inside the viewport rather than below the fold, a disabled primary is verified to drop the gradient and stay opaque, the gallery renders its cards in a uniform 4:3 crop, the category filter is verified to change the rendered results, both themes are measured to change the panel's surface and text colours, the prompt optimizer is verified present inside the prompt box, an idle panel is verified to show no phantom in-flight UI, a retry is verified to render its progress inside the failed record's own card after a full page reload (exactly one retrying card, zero placeholder cards, no duplicated background banner, the card count unchanged), and that attempt is followed through a real generation until it settles back into the same record, and the image viewer opens in-panel, covers the whole viewport with no containing-block trap, zooms by a measured layout change rather than a label, closes on Escape and on a backdrop click, does not close when the picture itself is clicked, steps through the gallery with the arrow keys while resetting the zoom per picture, and returns focus to the control that opened it. The suite was run twice: keyless (exercising the unconfigured branches, including the disabled primary's flat muted surface) and with a real key (the empty-prompt refusal branch plus the two retry checks, which start a real generation and follow it into the same record). Beyond the automated suite, real-key end-to-end runs against the live API verified the background-job and retry behaviours that cannot be asserted offline: a submitted image kept rendering after the panel was left and was still shown as running on return before settling into a result card; a failed video record retried successfully after a FULL page reload, with the card count unchanged (the row is updated in place); clicking retry on a failed record showed the progress only inside that card (no extra placeholder card, no background banner), and the same record then turned into the generated result in its original slot with the card count unchanged; and the prompt optimizer rewrote a draft and the undo restored the original text. Evidence: docs/evidence/isolated-mount-0.5.1.json, docs/evidence/browser-ui-check.json and docs/evidence/screenshots/. Cleanup verified: owned roots removed, all processes stopped. A finished picture can be continued: the panel restores its exact request, shows the source thumbnail, and submits the stored picture as the next request's reference — the Host inlines the bytes it already owns as a data: URI because the upstream cannot reach the authenticated same-origin media route. The browser suite therefore clicks 继续编辑 on a seeded picture, asserts the prompt came back, the source thumbnail is shown, the card count is unchanged and the submit button reads 生成修改版, then submits and follows a REAL data: URI image-to-image generation until the new version settles INTO the original's stack (card count unchanged) carrying its 承接 lineage, and finally reads the owned store to prove the new record keeps the symbolic reference and derivedFrom instead of freezing base64 into the index. A failed record instead restores only its prompt and parameters (调整后重试), which the offline suite covers for both capabilities; a finished video deliberately offers no continuation, because upstream has no video edit/extension endpoint and its reference-video input needs a public URL on the paid model. A continuation now JOINS its source instead of adding a sibling: the gallery groups records into lineages by derivedFrom, renders one photo-pile card per lineage with the newest version on the face and up to two neighbour strips beside it, and labels it with a version badge. The browser suite therefore asserts that a settled continuation leaves the card count UNCHANGED, produces exactly one pile with one fanned-out neighbour strip, measured to be outside the card's border box, above its shadow, and actually painting its own decoded picture; it then flips the pile with a REAL horizontal wheel gesture and requires the card box and the picture box to be identical before and after — the machine-checkable form of the reported flashing and shaking, which a jsdom test cannot measure — while requiring the flip to genuinely reach the older version, then swipes back and requires the newest version to return with the same box; it then clicks the version rail to PIN the older version and verifies the badge and rail follow, the pin survives the pointer leaving, the card height is unchanged, and clicking "1" returns to following the newest version; it then re-renders the pile in the OTHER theme and verifies the neighbour strip is still painting its own picture at a real width (the early theme screenshot is taken before any pile exists, so this is the only place the dark pile is ever looked at); finally it clicks 展开 and verifies every version becomes its own card, then 收起 and verifies the stack returns. A deep six-version lineage is then seeded and the page reloaded: the version rail must list six numbers with none clipped out of its box, the fan must stay capped at two strips, the badge must report six versions, the rail must reach the oldest version, and repeated real horizontal swipes must return to the newest version while keeping the card's measured box identical — the geometry guarantees must hold for a real editing chain, not only for a chain of two. The swipe is deliberately scoped to the picture, not the action row, so a card cannot change identity under a pointer that is about to click one of its buttons. Continuous retry is Host-owned: a retryable failure optionally starts a background loop with exponential backoff (15s doubling to a 180s cap, 5 attempts by default) that survives the panel being closed and reports its attempt number and next-attempt time through state(); only self-healing failures (queue full, rate limit, 5xx, timeout, broken download) are retried, a deterministic refusal is reported after one try, and the loop writes exactly one final record carrying its attempt count. The stack was then rebuilt a second time as a photo PILE, matching how a chat app shows several photos sent together, because the previous design announced its depth with decorative strips above the card and browsed with a vertical hover gesture that fought the pointer. Now the newest version is the print on the face of the pile, the neighbouring versions fan out to the LEFT and RIGHT as narrow strips carrying their OWN pictures, and the gesture is horizontal: a two-finger trackpad swipe (accumulated wheel delta, one flick per version), a pointer drag, or the arrow keys. The strips are absolutely positioned real elements in a gutter reserved on BOTH sides of the stage, at a z-index ABOVE the card, which is the only place that is outside the card's border box and still paints over the card's box shadow; both alternatives were built and rejected for observable reasons (as siblings BELOW the card the shadow paints them out; as a background or pseudo-element of the stage they are painted under the same shadow, i.e. drawn and invisible at once). The gutter is taken from outside the cell with a negative margin plus equal padding, so the front print keeps EXACTLY the width of every other card in the grid -- shrinking the card by the gutter re-flowed its action row onto a second line and made the pile a visibly different shape from its neighbours, which the browser suite now asserts by comparing measured widths. Flipping remains an opacity crossfade with no reflow: every version's shot and body stay mounted, all bodies share one grid cell, the picture is a fixed 4:3 box, and neither the card box nor the picture box may change by a single pixel across a swipe, a drag, an arrow key or a pinned jump -- all four are measured. A vertical wheel is deliberately NOT consumed (the gallery column must still scroll; the suite drives a real vertical wheel and requires no version change), the pile is clamped at both ends rather than wrapping, a drag suppresses the click that would otherwise open the viewer, and the native image drag is disabled because it takes over the gesture and fires pointercancel. The numbered rail still commits to a version, and the fan swaps sides with the committed version; a deep six-version lineage must keep all six rail numbers unclipped, cap the fan at two strips, and return to the newest version under repeated swipes without changing the card box.
